analysis.investment_thesis: Manyavar is a genuinely excellent business — 30.7% ROCE, 71.7% gross margins, near-zero capex — but at an earnings yield of ~5.1% (EBIT INR 575 Cr / EV ~INR 11,220 Cr), you are paying a steep premium that the Magic Formula simply cannot justify. The quality is there; the price is not.
key_strengths: Exceptional ROCE of 30.7% driven by asset-light franchise model with INR 3-4 Cr capex against INR 575 Cr EBIT — a textbook high-ROIC business.
Near-perfect FCF conversion: FCF of INR 385 Cr in FY25 vs net profit of INR 388 Cr — every rupee earned becomes cash.
Dominant brand moat in Indian celebration wear with 71.7% gross margins, far above typical apparel peers.
key_risks: Revenue has stalled — FY24 INR 1,368 Cr → FY25 INR 1,384 Cr (+1.2%), signalling saturation in core wedding wear category.
Operating income declining: INR 671 Cr (FY23) → INR 658 Cr (FY24) → INR 575 Cr (FY25), implying margin compression even as revenue treads water.
Finance costs surging 37.3% CAGR (INR 6 Cr → INR 55 Cr) from Ind AS 116 lease liabilities, masking true leverage from store expansion.
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~5.1% is well below the Magic Formula's 12% threshold — the stock fails the 'cheap' test decisively.
Two consecutive years of flat revenue with falling EBIT suggests the brand's growth runway may be narrowing faster than priced in.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Manyavar: EBIT for FY25 is INR 575 Cr against an Enterprise Value of roughly INR 11,220 Cr (market cap INR 10,753 Cr + debt INR 483 Cr – cash INR 17 Cr), yielding an earnings yield of just 5.1%. That is comfortably below my 6% minimum and miles from the 12–15% zone where I get excited. On the other side of the equation, ROIC is genuinely excellent — stated ROCE is 30.7%, corroborated by the absurdly low capex (INR 3–4 Cr/year) and near-100% FCF conversion. This is the kind of business quality I admire. But the Magic Formula demands BOTH cheap AND good; here you only have good.

What makes this harder to own at the current price is that the quality metrics are deteriorating at the margin. EBIT peaked at INR 671 Cr in FY23 and has since fallen 14% to INR 575 Cr in FY25, while revenue is essentially flat over two years. Finance costs have risen 8x since 2019, partly from lease accounting but still real cash obligations. The P/E of 26.7x and EV/EBITDA of 23.6x reflect a growth premium the business is no longer earning. I would revisit this seriously if the earnings yield approached 8–10% — roughly INR 280–350 price range — where the Magic Formula would give it a far better ranking.
